notes: Hand-run of the Book Scout research step (no admin credentials in the session, so the /run endpoint could not be used). Same rules as research.ts: available now on Kindle, attributed to a named human source, recent. Titles already sent in the June 2026 issues were excluded.

books.title: Heart of Glass
books.author: Jennifer Hillier
books.one_line: Twenty-five years after three teenage girls met a charming drifter at a Seaside, Washington amusement park, the man convicted as the Carnival Killer recants, reopening an old crime and starting a new one.

sources.name: The Poisoned Pen (Scottsdale) — Deb Lewis
sources.said: A twisty 'who really did it' with a satisfying ending that you root for long before you know it will come.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: Classic Jennifer Hillier, featuring an old crime, a new murder, and a whole lot of secrets.

books.title: The Blue Flame
books.author: George Pelecanos
books.one_line: Derek Strange, now in his seventies and retired from the force, takes on a case for a defense attorney in Washington, D.C., working it with questions and patience rather than technology; Pelecanos's first Strange novel in fourteen years.

sources.name: NPR — Maureen Corrigan
sources.said: Does for Washington, D.C., what Raymond Chandler did for LA… I hope it's never extinguished.

sources.name: The New York Times Book Review — Sarah Weinman
sources.said: A book about aging, and about the tools still at your disposal when youth is a long-ago memory.

sources.name: BookMarks (Literary Hub)
sources.said: Rated Rave on eight critic reviews, including Tom Nolan in the Wall Street Journal.

books.title: The Amateur
books.author: Chris Bohjalian
books.one_line: A 1970s moral fable that reworks Nabokov's classic into a slow-burning literary thriller about polite society and what it permits.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: Quite simply, a masterpiece. I cannot praise this novel enough. Delicate, haunting, complex, and startling; a wide-ranging condemnation of polite society.

sources.name: Kirkus Reviews — 20 Best Books to Read in August
sources.said: Nabokov's classic reinvented as a 1970s moral fable, with brilliantly developed characters and period detail.

books.title: All We Hide
books.author: Robyn Gigl
books.one_line: First in a new series: trans detective Lauren Kelly investigates the decades-old murder of a former high-school classmate while fighting discrimination inside her own department.

sources.name: The Poisoned Pen (Scottsdale) — Deb Lewis
sources.said: Filled with characters so real you might be tempted to reach out and give them a call. Excellent.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: The first in a new series featuring trans detective Lauren Kelly, as she fights rampant departmental discrimination.

books.title: Children of Wolves
books.author: Lawrence Osborne
books.one_line: A character study of expats and drifters at a seaside hotel in Turkey, with the action moving on to Istanbul.

sources.name: Kirkus Reviews — 20 Best Books to Read in August
sources.said: A quietly gripping novel that begs for a sequel.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: This time around, it's a seaside hotel in Turkey, with the action moving to Istanbul, as well.

books.title: You'll Be Sorry
books.author: Lisa Gardner
books.one_line: A standalone about a newlywed couple who move to a remote New Hampshire mountain town, an abandoned lodge, and a family of six who vanished thirty years earlier, until a dog starts digging.

sources.name: Kirkus Reviews
sources.said: Thriller maven Lisa Gardner's latest delivers small-town chills, New England style.

sources.name: The Poisoned Pen (Scottsdale)
sources.said: Featured as a store debut event in August.

books.title: One Good Eye
books.author: Kevin Wade
books.one_line: Second Jeep Mullane novel from the Blue Bloods showrunner, following his Edgar-nominated debut Johnny Careless.

sources.name: The Poisoned Pen (Scottsdale) — Deb Lewis
sources.said: Picked for August; John Sandford calls it a 'fast-moving classic crime novel.'

books.title: The Unknown
books.author: Riley Sager
books.one_line: A standalone set on a remote Vermont island that blends psychological suspense, gothic mystery, and a supernatural thread.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: Combining horror and mystery in a delightfully creepy, pastiche-savvy standalone.

books.title: God's Country
books.author: William Kent Krueger
books.one_line: The latest Cork O'Connor novel, in which Cork uncovers a conspiracy surrounding Minnesota's Boundary Waters.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: Cork uncovers a terrible conspiracy surrounding Minnesota's Boundary Waters.

books.title: The Intrigue
books.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
books.one_line: Noir in 1940s Veracruz: a con artist targets the owner of a small-town boardinghouse, and her niece demands half the take.

sources.name: NPR Books
sources.said: Recommended as an end-of-summer escape read alongside Richard Russo and George Pelecanos.

sources.name: Kirkus Reviews
sources.said: A rock-solid novel from a born storyteller. Clever, taut, and just flat-out fun.

books.title: Promised Land
books.author: Henry Wise
books.one_line: Sequel to Holy City: a missing-person case forces deputy sheriff Will Seems to confront how history anchors and corrupts the present in rural Virginia.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: Wise brings gothic notes to the classic detective plot, creating an atmosphere all his own.

books.title: The Secret Dinner
books.author: Raphael Montes (tr. Zoë Perry)
books.one_line: Broke roommates in Brazil make rent by hosting private dinners for the ultrawealthy, where the menu is human flesh.

sources.name: CrimeReads — Molly Odintz
sources.said: A group of broke roommates finds a novel way to make rent: hosting private dinners for the ultrawealthy, where they serve human flesh.
